terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the shop's stock runs on your store, a stop halfway through an order included.

tasks.title: Write a batch as one
tasks.description:
Implement `store.batch(changes)`: several changes made as one.

- `changes` is an array of `{ op: 'set', key, value }` and `{ op: 'delete', key }`; the store makes them in their order, and right after `batch` it holds all of them
- in the log, a store opened later sees all of the batch's changes or none of them, wherever a stop cut the file; every record before the batch is kept
- a batch cut short is left out like a record cut short, and cut off the file the same way, so the next change starts clean
- the promise resolves once the whole batch is in the file
- the format is yours; `compact()` keeps what a batch set

The format is yours, so the check judges by behaviour: it writes a batch, cuts `store.log` at every byte inside it, and opens your store on each, then changes it and opens it again.
nextSteps: Read "A batch has an end" in the lesson.
Choose what in the log says where a batch ends.
Write the batch with one `appendFile`, and make `decode` take its changes only when all of it is there.
Run `node src/try.js`: the order cut short should not be half taken.
hints: Writing a batch as its changes, one after another, means a stop between two of them leaves half the batch, and nothing in the file says anything was missing.
A record that says how many records follow, or one record that holds all the changes, lets the reader know where the batch ends, the same way a length tells where a value ends.
Write `` `batch ${changes.length}\n` `` followed by each change's record, in one `appendFile`. In `decode`, on a batch header read that many records; if any is not whole, the batch is not either.

tasks.title: Check a batch before writing it
tasks.description:
Make `batch` refuse a batch that is not right, before it writes anything.

- a batch that is not an array throws a `TypeError`
- so does a batch with any change that is not right: not an object, an `op` other than `set` or `delete`, a key that is missing or not text, or a set whose value is missing or not text
- a refused batch changes nothing at all: not the store, not the log, not even the good changes before the bad one
- an empty batch changes nothing, writes nothing and does not throw

The check gives your store batches with one bad change after good ones, and compares the store and the size of `store.log` before and after.
nextSteps: Try a batch whose last change has a number as its value: what is in the store afterwards?
Go through every change first, and throw at the first one that is not right.
Write and make the changes only when all of them passed.
hints: A batch that makes its first two changes before it notices the third is wrong is half a batch again, only made by your own code this time.
Two loops: one that only checks, then the write and one that changes. `Array.isArray` tells an array from anything else.

`if (!Array.isArray(changes)) throw new TypeError(...)`, then `for (const change of changes)` check `change?.op` and the types of `key` and `value`, then `if (changes.length === 0) return` before the write.

tasks.title: Keep the stock counts in your store
tasks.description:
Write the shop's stock functions in `src/stock.js` on the store.

- every function is given the store as `db`; a count is kept as text, the number in digits (`'1200'`)
- `stockOf(db, item)` returns the count as a number, `0` when the store has no such item
- `receive(db, item, count)` adds `count` to the item's stock
- `takeOrder(db, lines)`, for lines like `[{ item: 'card', count: 200 }]`, takes each line's count off its item as one batch: the whole order or none of it; an item may be on more than one line
- when any item has fewer than the order asks for, `takeOrder` throws an `Error` whose message names the item, and changes nothing
- the functions write no file themselves: every count lives in the store

The check runs your functions on a right store of its own, so this task does not depend on tasks 1 and 2. It reopens the store after each change, and cuts the store's log at every byte inside an order.
nextSteps: Read `src/old-stock.js` again: each change wrote the whole file. Here each change goes through the store.
Write `takeOrder`: work out every new count first, refuse if one would go below zero, then make them all in one batch.
hints: Two separate sets for one order are two records, and a stop between them takes half the order: exactly what Idris saw, in a new shape.
Count what each line leaves for the next one in a `Map` of item to count, starting each item from `stockOf`. `Number()` and `String()` turn text into a number and back.

Build the `Map`, throw `` new Error(`Not enough ${item}`) `` when a count would go below zero, then `await db.batch([...left].map(([item, count]) => ({ op: 'set', key: item, value: String(count) })))`.
